title: Past continuous: what was happening
goal: Set the scene of a story, and interrupt it
intro: The past continuous (was/were + -ing) describes an action in progress at a moment in the past: “At 9 pm I was cooking.” It’s perfect for the background of a story. A short past-simple action often interrupts it: “I was cooking when the lights went out.”

rules.rule: was/were + -ing for an action in progress in the past.
examples: At eight I was driving home.

rules.rule: Long action (was -ing) + when + short action (past simple).
examples: I was sleeping when you called.
She was walking home when it started to rain.

rules.rule: while + two long actions at the same time.
examples: While I was cooking, he was cleaning.
We were talking while they were eating.

mistakes.right: When you called, I was sleeping.
mistakes.why: The long background action takes was + -ing.
State verbs don’t take -ing, in the past either.

mistakes.wrong: While I cooked, the phone was ringing.
mistakes.right: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
mistakes.why: Long action: was -ing. Short action: past simple.

ex.q: I ___ a shower when the doorbell rang.
What ___ you doing at ten last night?
She was reading when the power ___.
While we ___ dinner, it started to rain.
When he entered, we watched a film.
ex.fixed: When he entered, we were watching a film.

ex.q: The kids was sleeping when we arrived.
ex.fixed: The kids were sleeping when we arrived.

ex.q: I was driving when I was seeing the accident.
ex.fixed: I was driving when I saw the accident.

ex.q: It ___ (rain) when we left the house.

ex.a: I was waiting for the bus when I saw her.

ex.q: Join with “when”: “I was cooking. My friend called.”
a: I was cooking when my friend called

talk: Tell a short story about something unexpected: what was happening, and then what happened. Use “I was … when …” at least twice.
